record.original_question: Let Σ_{n+1,2d} = C_0 ⊆ ··· ⊆ C_{k(n,d)-n} = P_{n+1,2d} be the filtration of cones of degree-2d forms in n+1 variables obtained from the Gram-matrix construction along projective varieties V_i containing the Veronese variety. For a strictly separating intermediate cone C_i appearing in the strict inclusions of filtration (6), determine a practical membership test for C_i, preferably one stated as an intrinsic property of a representing Gram matrix rather than by directly checking local positive semidefiniteness on the underlying variety.

evidence.quote: In this section, we pose some questions concerning membership tests for Ci’s, investigations of the dual cone C∨ i := {L ∈ Hom(R[X],R) | ∀f ∈ Ci : L(f) > 0} of Ci and generalizations of our considerations about Ci’s to cones along toric varieties.
Open Problem 1. Let Ci be a strictly separating intermediate cone in (6). Provide a membership test for Ci, preferably by an intrinsic property of a representing Gram matrix.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers n ≥ 1 and d ≥ 1, and let R[X] = R[x_0, x_1, …, x_n]_{2d} denote the finite-dimensional real vector space of homogeneous polynomials (forms) of degree 2d in n+1 variables. Inside R[X] consider:

• P_{n+1,2d} = { f ∈ R[X] : f(x) ≥ 0 for all x ∈ R^{n+1} }, the cone of positive semidefinite forms;
• Σ_{n+1,2d} = { f ∈ R[X] : f = ∑_j h_j^2, h_j ∈ R[x_0,…,x_n]_d }, the cone of sums of squares.

The Gram matrix method assigns to each form f ∈ R[X] the affine set
  G(f) = { A ∈ Sym_{k(n,d)}(R) : f = v_d(x)^T A v_d(x) },
where v_d(x) is the vector of all monomials of degree d in x_0, …, x_n and k(n,d) = (n+d choose d). Then f ∈ Σ_{n+1,2d} iff G(f) contains a positive semidefinite matrix.

Given a chain of projective subvarieties of P^{k(n,d)-1}
  ν_d(P^n) = V_0 ⊊ V_1 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ V_{k(n,d)-n} = P^{k(n,d)-1},
where ν_d denotes the Veronese embedding, define the intermediate cones
  C_i := { f ∈ R[X] : ∃ A ∈ G(f) with v^T A v ≥ 0 for all v ∈ V_i(R) }.
These satisfy
  Σ_{n+1,2d} = C_0 ⊆ C_1 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ C_{k(n,d)-n} = P_{n+1,2d}.

Assume the inclusion C_{i-1} ⊊ C_i is strict (the cone C_i is "strictly separating"). 

Problem: Provide a membership test for C_i — given a form f ∈ R[X], decide whether f ∈ C_i — preferably one formulated as an intrinsic algebraic property of a representing Gram matrix A ∈ G(f), rather than by directly verifying local positive semidefiniteness of A on the variety V_i.
artifact.category_tag: Positive semidefinite forms and Gram matrix cones
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a November 2024 preprint on separating cones defined by toric varieties. A web search found no subsequent work resolving it; the question of an intrinsic Gram-matrix membership test for the strictly separating intermediate cones appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Separating Cones defined by Toric Varieties: Some Properties and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: The paper applies the Gram matrix method to construct cones between Σ and P, introduces an intermediate cone filtration, and discusses the membership problem for these cones as an open question.
status_evidence.claim: The membership test for strictly separating intermediate cones C_i is explicitly listed as an open problem.
